Mutations leading to haploinsufficiency of GATA3 cause hypoparathyroidism, deafness, and renal disease. #### 1. heme oxygenase 1 deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.432)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6785807)

**Proposed mechanism:** GATA3 (HGNC:4160) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoparathyroidism (HP:0000940); GATA3 (HGNC:4160) —LEADS_TO→ Deafness (HP:0000365); GATA3 (HGNC:4160) —LEADS_TO→ Renal Disease (HP:0000109); GATA3 (HGNC:4160) —DISRUPTS→ Calcium Homeostasis (GO:0006970); HMOX1 (HGNC:4927) —DISRUPTS→ Heme (CHEBI:17644); Heme (CHEBI:17644) —DISRUPTS→ Oxidative Stress Response (GO:0006974); Oxidative Stress Response (GO:0006974) —DISRUPTS→ Calcium Homeostasis (GO:0006970); HMOX1 (HGNC:4927) —LEADS_TO→ Anemia (HP:0001924); HMOX1 (HGNC:4927) —LEADS_TO→ Jaundice (HP:0000952). Mutations in GATA3 lead to hypoparathyroidism, deafness, and renal disease, partly through disruption of calcium homeostasis. Loss-of-function mutations in HMOX1 impair heme breakdown, leading to increased oxidative stress, which in turn can disrupt calcium homeostasis, potentially exacerbating or contributing to the phenotypes seen in GATA3-related disorders.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that genetic variants in GATA3 do not affect calcium homeostasis pathways, or that HMOX1 deficiency has no impact on cellular oxidative stress levels or downstream calcium regulation in relevant cell types. _(variant: rs121918404 (GATA3 c.1360G>A, p.Gly454Ser) - AF=0.00004 in GnomAD exomes)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this overlap could inform therapeutic strategies for both conditions. For hypoparathyroidism-deafness-renal disease syndrome, interventions aimed at mitigating oxidative stress or supporting calcium regulation might be beneficial. For heme oxygenase 1 deficiency, therapies that specifically target calcium dysregulation could be explored.

#### 2. autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome type 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.415)

**Why it matters:** Targeting the FAS/FASLG pathway or downstream effectors of apoptosis could offer therapeutic avenues for ALPS-1.
